items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Methods, Challenges, Taxonomy, and Evaluation Practices
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract This systematic review made a bold attempt to examine artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications in drug discovery, addressing a fragmented literature characterized by inconsistent terminology and limited benchmarking. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science were queried (January 2019-August 2026). The three databases returned 23,404 records; after removing 4,491 duplicates and multi-stage screening, 618 peer-reviewed studies were included. Quality was assessed using a ROBINS-I-inspired framework across four dimensions (methodological rigor, dataset transparency, reproducibility, evaluation validity); 38 studies (6.1%) were double-coded (\((\kappa = 0.74)\)). Machine learning and deep learning dominated (99.8% and 78.0%, respectively). QSAR/CADD appeared in 58.9%, GNN/GCN in 45.1%, and Transformer/LLM architectures in 45.5%, with 99.8% of transformer papers published in 2024–2026. Virtual screening was most common (57.1%), followed by de novo design (30.6%) and drug-target interaction prediction (13.8%). The most prominent challenges were integration and clinical translation (15.2%), interpretability (11.3%), and benchmark/validation (9.2%). AUC-ROC dominated reporting (12.9%), while F1 (0.8%) and recall (0.5%) were severely under-reported-problematic for heavily imbalanced bioactivity datasets. items.title: LigRNA: High-accuracy prediction of RNA-ligand binding sites via dynamic chemical complementarity and language model encoding
items.abstract_or_text: RNA-binding small molecules represent a validated therapeutic modality, yet pinpointing their exact RNA binding sites remains critical for mechanistic understanding and drug optimization. Experimental methods, while precise, are costly and low-throughput, necessitating robust computational alternatives. Approaches based on static feature concatenation may overlook input-dependent relationships between RNA residues and ligand functional groups. Here we present LigRNA, a graph neural network framework that predicts RNA-ligand binding sites through joint cross-modal encoding of both molecules. LigRNA integrates structure-guided language model embeddings with physicochemical features-solvent-accessible surface area and secondary structure types, to construct comprehensive RNA representations. Ligands are encoded as attributed molecular graphs via graph attention networks, preserving atom-level chemical topology rather than compressing molecules into fixed fingerprints. A cross-attention mechanism then enables dynamic, ligand-dependent modulation of RNA nucleotide attention, capturing context-specific interaction patterns. Benchmarked on TE9 and TE18 datasets, LigRNA achieves F1 scores of 0.73 and 0.58, improving on GATRsite by 7.4% and 18.4%, respectively. Ablation studies identify the RNA residual encoder as the most consistent contributor across the two benchmarks. The source code is freely available at https://github.com/WillowWang0216/LigRNA.

items.title: RePurpose: An LLM-Assisted, Source-Traceable Drug Repurposing Tool with Retrospective Validation on Clemastine in Multiple Sclerosis
items.abstract_or_text: Summary: Thus far, evidence for drug repurposing is contained in target-, drug-, trial-, and literature-based data sources that are challenging to synthesize for non-specialists. Here, we introduce RePurpose, a web-based tool that takes as input a topic written in plain language and returns candidate drugs built from data in Open Targets, ClinicalTrials.gov, UniProt, and PubMed. For queries in the form of a goal, RePurpose filters candidate drugs by whether they modulate all targets implicated in the goal in the corresponding direction. Every candidate has a source that contributes evidence: a structured database, a clinical trial, or a proposal from a large language model. An adjustable ranking adjusts the order of candidates from well-studied to less well-known candidate drugs. We retrospectively tested RePurpose with the trial drug clemastine, which was being considered as a remyelinating agent in multiple sclerosis (MS). RePurpose retrieved clemastine in each replicate of the mechanism-worded queries, but in no replicates of the disease-worded queries, and no structured query retrieved it without the language model enabled. Its ranked outputs reflected the evidence supporting clemastine but not later evidence of harm in progressive MS, which was reachable only through an on-demand literature search. Our results imply that RePurpose may be better at tracing evidence around a hypothesis than generating new hypotheses. Availability and Implementation RePurpose Pharma is freely accessible at https://www.repurposepharma.com/. For code and more information on the application, see: https://github.com/nayagamnitin-hub/RePurpose-Pharma.

items.title: NAD + /NADH as the Electrochemical Currency and Other Specific Electron Transfer Molecules in Health and Disease
items.abstract_or_text: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, in its oxidized (NAD+) and reduced (NADH) forms, is a central metabolic cofactor that links cellular energy production to a wide array of signaling processes, including DNA repair, chromatin regulation, calcium signaling, and circadian control. Beyond its classical role as an electron carrier in redox reactions of glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation via Complex I of the electron transport chain), NAD+ serves as an obligate substrate for several classes of non-redox enzymes. These include the sirtuin family, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs), the ectoenzymes CD38/CD157, and SARM1. This dual functionality positions NAD+ as a key convergence point between metabolism and cell signaling. NAD+/NADH metabolism is highly dynamic and compartmentalized. Distinct subcellular pools exist in the mitochondria, cytosol, and nucleus, with very limited free exchange of the dinucleotide itself across the inner mitochondrial membrane. The NAD⁺/NADH ratio—rather than total pool size alone—serves as a critical readout of cellular redox state: cytosolic ratios are normally high (favoring oxidative metabolism and glycolysis), while mitochondrial ratios are lower. Both the ratio and absolute levels fluctuate with age, diet, nutrient availability, oxygen tension, and other contextual factors, yet remain tightly regulated through biosynthetic pathways (de novo from tryptophan, Preiss–Handler from nicotinic acid, and the dominant salvage pathway via NAMPT) and consumption by the enzymes noted above. Disruption of NAD+ homeostasis is now recognized as a hallmark of aging and a contributor to multiple age-related pathologies. Age-associated declines in NAD⁺ levels and shifts in the NAD⁺/NADH ratio impair mitochondrial function, sirtuin activity, DNA repair, and stress resistance, while promoting senescence, inflammation, and metabolic inflexibility. Altered NAD⁺ metabolism is equally prominent in cancer. Tumor cells frequently upregulate NAD⁺-salvage enzymes (especially NAMPT) to expand the total NADH pool, support high glycolytic flux through continuous NAD⁺ regeneration (primarily via lactate dehydrogenase), maintain redox balance, and enhance resistance to genotoxic stress via PARP activity. Compartment-specific changes are also critical: reverse electron transport (RET) at Complex I, enriched in certain cancer stem cells (e.g. glioma stem cells), lowers the mitochondrial NAD⁺/NADH ratio. This inhibits SIRT3, stabilizes HIF-1α, and sustains stemness programs (e.g. SOX2), thereby favoring tumor progression and therapy resistance. NADH reductive stress more broadly can drive metabolic reprogramming that supports proliferation and survival.This review examines the biochemistry and subcellular compartmentalization of NAD⁺/NADH metabolism, its physiological roles in healthy cells, the mechanisms by which malignant cells reprogram NAD⁺ metabolism to their advantage (including RET-driven redox shifts), and the therapeutic strategies currently under investigation. These range from NAMPT inhibitors (which face challenges of limited single-agent efficacy and dose-limiting toxicities in clinical trials) and NAD⁺-boosting precursors (nicotinamide riboside, nicotinamide mononucleotide, and related compounds) to agents that modulate Complex I/RET or other nodes of NAD⁺ homeostasis, with the goal of exploiting or correcting these alterations in aging and cancer.

items.title: A safety aware framework for conversational health agents integrating fuzzy logic reinforcement learning and large language models with self determination theory and constrained optimization called SAFE CHA
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract A hybrid conversational health agent (CHA) is proposed that integrates large language models (LLMs), fuzzy logic, and reinforcement learning (RL) to support mental health dialogue. Mental disorders are estimated to affect nearly 970 million people worldwide, yet clinical support remains limited and inaccessible for many. Although chatbots have been introduced to improve accessibility, a balance among empathy, personalization, and safety must still be achieved. In this work, a hybrid architecture was designed in which (1) user affect and intent are analyzed by an LLM; (2) a fuzzy inference layer maps noisy affective signals into interpretable low-dimensional state vectors; (3) an RL agent determines high-level dialogue strategies through Self-Determination Theory (SDT)-shaped rewards; (4) a calibrated risk monitor enforces safety through escalation; and (5) an outer-loop optimizer tunes fuzzy sets, prompts, and RL hyperparameters under safety constraints. Formal derivations, component algorithms, and computational complexity analyses are provided. Evaluation metrics are defined in terms of empathy, engagement, SDT alignment, fairness, and risk. A reference implementation using NumPy and Matplotlib is made available to reproduce all figures. By combining interpretability through fuzzy logic, adaptability through RL, and fluency through LLMs, a safe, human-aligned conversational system is enabled. Comparative experiments with rule-based, fuzzy-only, LLM-only, and RL-only agents are reported to highlight trade-offs among control, safety, and learning. The proposed hybrid approach is expected to serve as a blueprint for explainable and safe mental health dialogue systems.

items.title: A systematic investigation of molecular encoding methods for drug property predictions across neural network and Transformer encoder-based model
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Fundamental investigations into how different molecular encoding methods affect molecular property prediction remain relatively limited. In this study, we extensively examined the optimal molecular encoding methods for molecular properties prediction using two prevalent structure designs: neural network model (MLP) and a Transformer encoder-based model (MLP + TL). For molecular encoding methods, we investigated several types of fingerprints, including traditional topological fingerprints, substructure-based fingerprints, and string-based representations. These two models were trained on seven well-known molecular datasets to evaluate different input molecular encoding methods based on evaluation metrics. On several biologically relevant classification tasks, including toxicity, mutagenicity, and side-effect prediction, our models consistently achieved average AUC values above 0.9. Beyond model performance, we further explored whether the Transformer encoder-based framework could provide interpretable insight. Rather than relying on external post-hoc explanation methods such as the local interpretable model-agnostic explanation (LIME) or the Deep SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we leveraged the model’s intrinsic attention weights as an internal interpretability signal for identifying potentially important feature. To further support this analysis, we conducted case studies on the BBBP and MUTAG datasets. The MLP + TL model using MACCS and PubChem as input can capture chemically interpretable groups that determined the major blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and mutagenicity in Salmonella typhimurium . In particular, a comparison between Morphine and Heroin highlighted the role of hydroxyl-related substructures in BBB permeability prediction, which was consistently reflected in the attention weights. Overall, our findings provide practical guidance for selecting effective molecular encoding methods and contribute to the development of interpretable molecular informatics approaches for drug discovery.

items.title: Beyond Better Models: Barriers and a Path Forward in Generalisable TCR Antigen Specificity Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: T cells are at the centre of adaptive immunity, protecting the organism against infection and cancer. T cell receptors (TCRs), expressed on the surface of T cells, enable the recognition of target cells through interactions with peptides presented by major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) molecules. Reliable, large-scale mapping of TCRs to their cognate pMHCs remains a holy grail of modern systems immunology, with far-reaching implications for cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and the understanding and treatment of autoimmune diseases. While exhaustive experimental mapping remains intractable due to the enormous combinatorial sequence space of TCRs and pMHCs, computational approaches offer a promising alternative. Consequently, we have witnessed increasingly sophisticated computational models of TCR antigen specificity, from small neural networks to deep generative models and large protein language models. However, several independent benchmarks have shown that these models, despite their size and sophistication, largely fail to generalise to TCRs or pMHCs not present in the data available during model development. Here, we investigate possible reasons for this and suggest a path forward to generalisable TCR:pMHC prediction. First, our analysis of the largest public repositories of TCR:pMHC data reveals significant biases towards a small number of antigens and MHC molecules, sparse sampling of TCR sequence space per pMHC, as well as inconsistencies and inaccuracies in data collation. Second, we show the importance of carefully setting up model evaluation to measure discrimination based on antigen specificity instead of confounding factors present in the evaluation data. Finally, we highlight the need for and propose how best to match the evaluation metric with the specific downstream application of the predictions. Our investigation suggests that we, as a community, need more representative and better curated data, and a robust set of metrics and benchmarks to guide future model development towards generalisable TCR:pMHC specificity prediction.

items.title: Governable agentic intelligence: a lifecycle framework linking capability, assurance, and oversight in large language model agents
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) embeds large language models (LLMs) in action loops in which they plan, retrieve evidence, invoke tools, maintain memory, coordinate with other agents, and change external state. Reviews of this field have proliferated, yet they remain fragmented: architecture surveys catalogue components, evaluation surveys catalogue benchmarks, and safety surveys catalogue risks, while deployed agents couple all three. Scholars have yet to sufficiently examine how capability, evaluation, and governance interact within the lifecycle of a single agentic system. We address this gap through a critical review that codes 19 reviews and surveys published in Artificial Intelligence Review between 2024 and 2026 and situates them within foundational primary studies and cross-venue surveys. We argue that agency is a configurable property of a socio-technical control loop, not an attribute of a model. From the corpus, we develop the Agentic Intelligence Lifecycle (AIL), a six-layer framework spanning foundation, cognition, grounding, orchestration, evaluation, and governance. Our central finding is that every mechanism that expands capability also incurs an assurance debt : a gap between the risks the mechanism introduces and the controls that keep those risks observable and bounded. We theorize this relationship in five propositions, propose a five-question assurance model that shifts evaluation from outputs to trajectories and deployment conditions, and derive a ten-point research agenda for agentic systems that are observable, attributable, interruptible, and governable.

items.title: Entropy-driven adaptive neural architecture search for cell segmentation on edge devices
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Accurate and real-time segmentation of cells in microscopy images is a critical task in biomedical research. Incubator-like edge devices are increasingly being used for real-time monitoring of cellular activities, facilitating timely intervention, which is particularly important when studying dynamic cellular processes. However, adapting to the deployment requirements of diverse edge devices, particularly those with limited resources, presents significant challenges in network architecture design. This requires considering resource constraints and hardware metrics associated with different edge devices, necessitating rigorous control of model complexity and resource utilisation. To address these challenges, we propose a hardware-aware neural architecture search method based on the U-Net backbone to segment various cell types. By incorporating hardware-based penalty terms and an entropy-driven mechanism, our method optimizes the search strategy to maximize segmentation accuracy while ensuring compatibility with target hardware. We evaluated our approach on five resource-constrained hardware platforms and achieved competitive segmentation performance on ten 2D live-cell imaging datasets from the Cell Tracking Challenge, while maintaining favourable hardware efficiency.

items.title: Agrifusion: An Agentic Multimodal Framework for Explainable and Multilingual Agricultural Decision Intelligence
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Agricultural productivity in developing regions is constrained by fragmented decision-support systems, limited multilingual accessibility, and the absence of integrated explainable intelligence. Existing solutions typically address crop recommendation, plant disease detection, and conversational advisory as separate tasks, without providing unified multimodal reasoning. This work presents Agrifusion, an agentic multimodal framework that integrates structured crop prediction, visual disease classification, explainability propagation, multilingual reasoning, and voice interaction within a cohesive agricultural intelligence system. The proposed architecture coordinates specialized agents for tabular modeling, image-based inference, interpretability generation, and large language model (LLM) reasoning. Interpretability mechanisms, including Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), feature attribution, and Grad-CAM visualization, are directly propagated into multilingual advisory prompts, ensuring transparent and traceable recommendations. The disease classification was performed using EfficientNet-B3. The framework further incorporates speech-to-text and text-to-speech modules supporting six Indian languages, enabling voice-first agricultural interaction. Structured soil–climate features are processed using optimized ensemble and deep learning models, achieving macro F1-score of 0.9977. Plant disease classification on the PlantDoc dataset demonstrates robust generalization under real-field variability, achieving an F1-score of 0.9028. Word Error Rates (WER) ranged from 0.05 to 0.10 across languages, while Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) scores above 4.5/5 for usability, clarity, trustworthiness, and language accessibility. However, because the crop results are unusually high for a public tabular dataset, the proposed study explicitly treats them as dataset-specific preliminary results and identifies duplicate checking, leakage-controlled preprocessing, nested model selection, and external validation as necessary safeguards. End-to-end multimodal inference operates within practical latency constraints on both Central Processing Unit (CPU) and Graphical Processing Unit (GPU) environments. By unifying predictive modeling, explainability, multilingual reasoning, and speech interaction within a deployable agentic architecture, Agrifusion advances beyond modular agricultural Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools toward a scalable deployment-oriented prototype decision-support ecosystem. End-to-end latency was 4.78s on CPU and 2.11s on GPU. The results support the feasibility of an evidence-aware, explainable, multilingual agricultural decision-support architecture while highlighting the need for stronger external and field validation.

items.title: T-cell dysregulation is implicated in the encephalopathy of prematurity
items.abstract_or_text: Preterm birth is strongly linked to systemic inflammation and encephalopathy of prematurity, which underlies subsequent cognitive impairment. T-cell immunity contributes to brain-immune crosstalk across the life course but its role in the pathogenesis of encephalopathy of prematurity is unknown. Protein epigenetic scores are DNA methylation (DNAm)-based proxies of circulating proteins. We tested the hypothesis that T-cell dysregulation has a specific role in child neurodevelopment following preterm birth. Multimodal data were collected from 144 preterm infants (median gestational age at birth 29+5 weeks [range 23+3 to 32+6]) recruited to a prospective cohort study: saliva DNAm for protein epigenetic score derivation and brain MRI, both at term-equivalent age, and the Mullen Scales of Early Learning Composite score at 5 years from a subset. We investigated associations of the epigenetic scores for cytotoxic and regulatory T cell-associated molecule (DNAm CRTAM) and C-reactive protein (DNAm CRP; a non-specific marker of inflammation) with MRI metrics of encephalopathy of prematurity: global and regional brain volumes, and general factors of diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging metrics averaged across 42 white matter tracts. We tested whether DNAm CRTAM explains more variance than DNAm CRP in MRI metrics of the encephalopathy of prematurity and cognitive scores in childhood. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower general factor of fractional anisotropy ({beta} = -0.252, q = 0.011) and higher general factors of radial diffusivity ({beta} = 0.215, q = 0.039), mean diffusivity ({beta} = 0.198, q = 0.047) and orientation dispersion index ({beta} = 0.201, q = 0.048), independent of inflammatory morbidities and other biological covariates after false discovery rate correction. DNAm CRTAM explained more variance than DNAm CRP (maximum incremental R2 = 4.2% vs 1.5%) in diffusion MRI metrics. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower cognitive scores at 5 years, independent of DNAm CRP and other covariates ({beta} = -0.332, P = 0.008), and explained more variance in cognitive scores than DNAm CRP (incremental R2 = 9.4% vs 1.2%). An epigenetic proxy of CRTAM in preterm infants is associated with both encephalopathy of prematurity in the neonatal period and lower cognitive performance at 5 years, explaining greater incremental variance than a non-specific marker of inflammation. The data implicate T-cell dysregulation in the pathophysiology of atypical neurodevelopment following preterm birth.

items.title: Federated Deep Learning for Privacy-Preserving Data Fusion in Sustainable AI-Driven Healthcare Systems
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract The growing volume and complexity of heterogeneous medical data create challenges in extracting diagnostic knowledge while preserving privacy because centralized models face high computation costs and security risks. To overcome this limitation, the novel Asynchronous Federated Multi-Convolution Spatial and Efficient Squeeze-Excitation Network (AFL-MCSESEN) with Bulyan-Based Adaptive Differential Privacy (BADP) was proposed for Privacy-Preserving Multi-Modal Data Fusion in Sustainable AI-Driven Healthcare Systems (HS) (AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS). Initially, Multi-modal data such as structured, semi-structured, and unstructured Knee Osteoarthritis data are collected and stored in Apache Spark managed by data lake. These heterogeneous sources are integrated using the Unified Element Tree Fusion method. Then, these fused data are processed through Z-score normalization and feature vector encoding. Simultaneously, the knee joint images are standardized for attaining consistent visual representation of pathological changes. Then, these pre-processed inputs are processed for Local Feature Extraction and Refinement using a Multi-Convolution Spatial and Efficient Squeeze-Excitation Network. Here, ResNet-34 backbone integrated with a Condensed Depthwise Squeeze-Excitation (CDSE) module and Multi-Convolution Spatial Attention (MCSA) was utilized to isolate subtle clinical indicators. To maintain institutional privacy, these features are trained within an privacy-preserving asynchronous federated learning framework, where ten institutional clients compute local gradients on vertically partitioned data using secure inner-product evaluations. Finally, a Bulyan-Based Adaptive Differential Privacy mechanism is utilized for further enhancing robustness and privacy. By this, the proposed AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS system provide sustainable, high-accuracy diagnostic tool for classifying Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) Grades of Knee Osteoarthritis such as Grade 0 (Healthy), Grade 1 (Doubtful), Grade 2 (Mild), Grade 3 (Moderate) and Grade 4 (Severe). Here, the proposed AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS system attains an Accuracy of 99.64%, an Area Under curve value as 0.998, Communication Overhead as 285MB, Data Integration Latency as 703.33ms, Spark Query Throughput as 516.67QPS, Attack Success Rate as 1.8 and Privacy-Utility Index (PUTI) as 0.96. By this results, the proposed AFL-MCSESEN-BADP-HS system provides the promising solution for Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Systems.

items.title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Psychosocial Assessment of Women's Mental Health and Empowerment
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Women’s mental health is an important public health concern that significantly impacts their overall well-being and quality of life. Among several mental health challenges, depression is one of the most common conditions affecting women, while maternal depression presents additional psychological challenges during pregnancy and the postpartum period. These conditions are influenced by multiple social, economic, psychological, and empowerment-related factors, making their accurate assessment challenging. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches are offers effective means of identifying hidden patterns and predicting women’s mental health outcomes. Moreover, existing methodologies have limited capability to explain how empowerment and psychosocial factors influence women’s mental health, highlighting the need for an explainable framework. To overcome these challenges, this research work develops an Explainable Women's Mental Health and Empowerment Assessment (X-WMHEA) model using psychosocial factors for effective analysis. The proposed model utilizes HSIC-LASSO to identify informative and non-redundant psychosocial factors by recognizing their dependencies with the target outcomes. Moreover, the TabM model learns complex relationships among the selected psychosocial factors and classify women’s mental health conditions. In addition, the Adan optimizer is utilized to refine the model parameters and enhance the convergence of the learning process. To enhance model transparency, the SHAP is integrated to quantify the contribution of individual psychosocial factors and provide meaningful insights into factors associated with women's mental health and empowerment. The performance of the proposed X-WMHEA model demonstrates superior performance, achieving accuracy of 95.53% and 96.75% on the Women Depression Dataset and Maternal Depression Dataset. Additionally, an ablation study is conducted to examine the contribution of each component in the proposed framework. Thus, the proposed model provides an effective and interpretable approach for analyzing psychosocial factors associated with women’s mental health and empowerment, supporting reliable assessment and informed decision-making.

items.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
items.abstract_or_text: With people increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, the need to evaluate these tools is becoming more pressing. Recent benchmarks attempt to mimic a realistic setting by simulating multi-turn interactions with synthetic patients and evaluating them with an LLM-as-a-judge. However, the usefulness of these methods is limited because simulated patients can be overly forthcoming and self-reflective, and judgments typically involve opaque Likert scales with unclear practical utility. To bridge these gaps, we introduce MindEval2, an evaluation framework that consists of two components: Mental Health Quality Rubrics (MHQR), for evaluation, and MindSim, for patient simulation. For MHQR, we collaborate with PhD-level psychologists to develop a set of rubrics that break down response quality into explicit operational criteria that are more interpretable and actionable than existing evaluation taxonomies. MindSim, in turn, is an LLM harness that combines carefully-designed patient profiles with tools, enabling more varied, challenging, and realistic interactions than existing baselines. The harness also contains a memory component that is updated between each interaction, enabling MindEval2 to model the longitudinal aspect of mental health. We evaluate 18 proprietary and open-weight models on MindEval2, finding that while frontier models have largely improved on issues related to surface level quality and boundaries, guidance calibration remains the dominant failure mode across all models, accounting for most of the quality gap.

items.title: Spurious Attention Heads in Vision Transformers: Mechanistic Identification of Annotation-Driven Bias in Medical Chest X-Ray Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Vision Transformers deployed in medical imaging exploit spurious correlations, yet the internal mechanisms remain unidentified and impossible to fix. We apply mechanistic interpretability to locate one such mechanism in ViT-Base 16: a single attention head (L8H10) that functions as a dedicated annotation-reader on chest X-rays, attending to corner text rather than lung pathology in 62% of 200 COVID-19 images. Causal validation via inpainting confirms annotation content rather than luminance or edge density drives the behaviour, increasing lung attention 1.52 times upon removal in affected images (p{<}0.0001). The finding replicates across NIH ChestX-ray14 (79%), DeiT-Base (88%), and ViT-Large 16 (80%), establishing spurious annotation-attending heads as a consistent property of ViT-family architectures across two datasets and three architectures. Full fine-tuning does not suppress the behaviour and may entrench it: 98.4% of spurious images remain spurious and the spurious rate rises marginally, as the shortcut is reinforced rather than removed. Critically, single-head ablation produces p{=}0.340 and multi-head ablation of all three identified carriers produces p{=}0.532, meaning a causally verified annotation-reading circuit is completely invisible to output-level evaluation. Mechanistic auditing finds what behavioural testing cannot.

items.title: Scalable Enzyme Reaction Retrieval Enables Metagenomic Biocatalyst Discovery
items.abstract_or_text: Enzyme catalyzed reactions drive metabolism and enable diverse applications in biotechnology and sustainable synthesis, but assigning catalytic functions to uncharacterized enzymes and finding enzymes for target reactions remain major challenges. Despite recent advances in machine learning, translating enzyme function prediction into systematic discovery across the vast space of uncharacterized proteins and biochemical reactions remains challenging. Here we present EzHit, a lightweight framework for bidirectional enzyme reaction retrieval. Across enzyme annotation, orphan-reaction retrieval and family-specific fine-tuning benchmarks, EzHit achieved strong top-ranked performance and outperformed representative enzyme reaction matching baselines. We further show that Mahalanobis distance based geometric confidence provides more useful reliability estimates than probability-derived uncertainty metrics or evidential learning, enabling confidence-aware prioritization of high scoring candidates. Owing to its efficiency, EzHit was applied to a nearly trillion-scale OMG_Prot50 with RHEA screen, yielding 8.20 billion retained enzyme reaction associations across 30.27 million predicted enzyme sequences. Experimental validation further confirmed the activity of EzHit prioritized metagenomic enzyme candidates for a sparsely annotated reaction. Together, these results establish EzHit as a scalable framework for enzyme annotation, reaction-guided mining and biocatalyst discovery

items.title: AMMPER-2: A spatially explicit agent-based model of microbial radiobiology with redox dye simulation
items.abstract_or_text: To reduce health risks for human space exploration, it is important to model the effects of deep-space radiation on biological systems. The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a common model organism in space radiobiology, but little is known about how radiation damage to individual cells translates into the population-level effects that experiments measure. The Agent-Based Model for Microbial Populations Exposed to Radiation (AMMPER) is a spatially explicit agent-based model that simulates the effects of ionizing radiation on S. cerevisiae cells and produces population-level results. Its goal is to improve experiment design and data interpretation. AMMPER-1 demonstrated that agent-based simulations can qualitatively reproduce the effects of proton radiation on the growth rate of wild-type and DNA-repair mutant yeast. Here, we present AMMPER-2, which addresses limitations of the first model and expands its capabilities. AMMPER-2 incorporates the dynamics of the redox dye alamarBlue, a data type commonly generated in spaceflight microbiology experiments, and models the fate of reactive oxygen species in more detail. It also adds an improved graphical interface and runs faster. AMMPER-2 remains easy to execute in Python on a standard personal laptop, providing space biologists a tool to explore experimental conditions, generate hypotheses, and interpret data from microbial space radiation experiments.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning for Molecule Design: A Taxonomy of Algorithms, Benchmarks, and Road to Synthesizable Leads
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been in the forefront in traversing the vast chemical space for novel drug discovery. In this survey, we discuss the landscape of applying RL in two related paradigms: de novo drug design, the process of generating novel drugs from scratch and drug structure optimization, an approach to enhance the drug-likeness of an existing drug, with a case study for the latter.We describe the field along a taxonomy spanning value-based, policy-gradient, reward-proportional, and search-based methods, highlighting how molecular representation methods have evolved from pioneering RNN-based approaches to the latest transformer-based language models. Language models are treated as a cross-cutting layer across these families, most recently as agents that acton a molecule through chemical tools. We critically assess the frequently used datasets for training the models and benchmarks to evaluate the performance of those models across various drug generation and structure optimization tasks, arguing that strong benchmark performance does not always translate into real-world utility. We also showcase the recurrent challenges in modeling drugdesign algorithms and possible mitigation, with a final discussion on the overall developmental landscape in this field with future prospects.

items.title: VALCON: Benchmarking and Enhancing Value Consistency in Large Language Models via Dual-Role Variation
items.abstract_or_text: Current value alignment evaluations for large language models (LLMs) heavily rely on output compliance, overlooking whether LLMs maintain value consistency when alternating between generator and evaluator roles. Such consistency is increasingly important because modern LLM agents and alignment pipelines often rely on the same LLM to both generate actions and evaluate their acceptability. To mitigate this limitation, we propose VALCON, a role-driven data construction framework that operationalizes value consistency into three benchmark suites (VAB-Consistency, VAB-Boundary, VAB-Challenge) via dual-role variation. By systematically pairing an LLM's generative behavior with its evaluative judgments under identical principles, VALCON synthesizes target evaluation data that exposes hidden value discrepancies. Experiments on 28 LLMs reveal pervasive cross-role inconsistency: models with highly compliant outputs frequently fail to align their judgments with their own generations. To understand and address this gap, we perform mechanistic probing that uncovers a role-dependent representational decoupling associated with this behavioral asymmetry. Guided by these insights, we propose a representation-directed intervention that effectively mitigates consistency failures. Our work establishes value consistency as a distinct alignment dimension and provides a complete evaluation-analysis-mitigation pipeline. Code and data are available at https://github.com/tjunlp-lab/VALCON.

items.title: Investigating the Ligandin Activity of Schistosoma mansoni Glutathione S-Transferases Toward Testosterone: Implications for Novel Anthelminthic Drug Target Discovery
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Schistosomiasis is one of the most common neglected tropical diseases globally, with more than 250 million people affected, and praziquantel is the only broadly available chemotherapeutic agent. However, concerns regarding decreased susceptibility to the drug and the lack of alternative therapies underscore the need to identify new therapeutic targets. Glutathione S -transferases (GSTs) are enzymes with diverse biological functions, including parasite detoxification, antioxidant defense, and ligand transport. This study investigated the interaction of 26- and 28-kDa GST isoforms from Schistosoma species with testosterone, which was evaluated as a potential anthelmintic. Testosterone did not exhibit acute vermicidal activity, as adult Schistosoma mansoni worms remained motile after 60 min, whereas praziquantel caused immediate complete immobilization. Homology models of S. mansoni Sm 26GST and Sm 28GST were validated by Ramachandran analysis and showed conserved catalytic cores with variable substrate-binding loops. Recombinant Sj 26GST and Sh 28GST were successfully overexpressed and purified. Both enzymes were inhibited by testosterone in a concentration-dependent manner, with IC₅₀ values of 0.63 mM and 0.73 mM, respectively. Far-UV Circular dichroism and extrinsic ANS fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed the conformational changes caused by the ligands. Induced-fit docking showed that the binding pocket is conserved at the GST dimer interface, and the 500-ns molecular dynamics simulations showed that the complexes were more stable than the apo proteins, with Sm 28GST being more rigid. Testosterone analogues were identified by high-throughput virtual screening that predicted binding affinities higher than those of testosterone. The results suggest that schistosome GSTs are promising targets for structure-based drug discovery against schistosomes.

items.title: Benchmarking Recording-Level Clinical Speech De-identification for Privacy-Preserving Clinical Audio
items.abstract_or_text: Transcript-based de-identification protects textual records but leaves sensitive health information (SHI) directly audible in source recordings, limiting trustworthy reuse of clinical audio. However, standardized evaluations of recording-level SHI detection remain limited. We established the SREDH-AICUP 2025 benchmark to evaluate recording-level SHI detection systems and characterize the approaches. All 22 qualifying systems combined automatic speech recognition with downstream SHI detection, whereas we additionally evaluated end-to-end detection from audio. Pipeline baselines outperformed the end-to-end baseline in transcription (MER, 0.123 vs 0.155) and SHI detection (macro-F1, 0.507-0.653 vs 0.422). Synthetic Mandarin speech-text augmentation enabled the end-to-end model to detect Mandarin SHI that was not identified without augmentation (macro-F1, 0.171 vs 0). Foundation models showed category-specific differences in SHI recognition, and type-aware adaptive routing improved macro-F1 from 0.656 to 0.697. These findings establish standardized reference performance, characterize current system designs, and demonstrate how language-specific augmentation and category-aware model integration can improve recording-level SHI detection.

items.title: Neural signatures of glioma progression using implanted neural interfaces
items.abstract_or_text: High-grade glioma is an incurable brain cancer with a median survival of approximately 14 months. Over the last 50 years, small improvements in patient outcomes have been overshadowed by significant progress in most other cancers. Yet, emerging research has revealed that neural circuits play an active and central role in driving glioma growth and proliferation, highlighting the nervous system as a promising avenue for both disease monitoring and therapeutic intervention. Here, we present a platform for chronically monitoring tumor progression using neural recordings in freely behaving mice with gliomas. Using this platform across multiple mouse strains and glioma models, we show that neural recordings can accurately track tumor progression in vivo. Cancer progression was consistently associated with elevated gamma-band neural activity in the tumor microenvironment across both adult glioblastoma (GBM) and pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) cancer models. Interestingly, lower frequency neural activity exhibited distinct, cell-line specific changes over time: GBM models exhibited decreases in low frequency neural activity whereas DIPG models exhibited increases over time. Finally, using machine learning models applied to chronic neural recordings from tumor-bearing mice treated with or without standard-of-care chemotherapy (temozolomide for GBM), we accurately predicted tumor burden as inferred through in vivo bioluminescence imaging. By fitting low-dimensional mathematical models to gamma-band neural trajectories, we could further predict individual tumor growth rates over a 5-week period with high accuracy. These results establish that pathological neural-tumor interactions can be harnessed to monitor glioma progression in vivo. Coupling this monitoring capability with therapeutic electrical stimulation in the same device could open up a new class of implantable, closed-loop neurotechnologies with the potential to transform glioma treatment.

items.title: Evolutionarily Conserved Plasmodium falciparum HSP70-3 Enhances the Immunogenicity of the Established Malaria Vaccine Antigen Circumsporozoite Protein through Cross-Presentation
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Clinically approved P. falciparum circumsporozoite protein (PfCSP)-based pre-erythrocytic stage malaria vaccines suffer from sub-optimal efficacy and rapidly waning memory. By decoding these limitations, we fast-tracked vaccine optimization by correcting CSPs fragile immunogenicity using a parasite-derived chaperone. Unlike other orthologues of P. falciparum heat shock protein 70 (PfHSP70), substrate-binding domain (SBD) of PfHSP70-3 is an evolutionarily conserved internal mitochondrial matrix chaperone. We demonstrate that PfHSP70-3-SBD hydrophobic region complexes with PfCSP and targets host CD91 on antigen-presenting cells to trigger cross-presentation, resulting in enhanced immune responses to PfCSP. Methods: In silico analyses predicted interactions among PfHSP70-3-SBD, PfCSP, and CD91 receptor. Recombinant PfHSP70-3-SBD and PfCSP proteins were purified and assessed for in vitro interaction using ELISA and far-western dot blot assays. BALB/c mice were immunized with alum-formulated PfCSP, with or without PfHSP70-3-SBD. PfCSP-specific IgG and IFN-{gamma} expression were evaluated by ELISA and RT-qPCR, respectively. Functional activity was assessed using transgenic Plasmodium berghei expressing PfCSP (Pb/Pf CSP), by sporozoite neutralization assay. Findings: PfHSP70-3-SBD demonstrated a specific interaction with PfCSP. The complex primarily engages CD91 receptor cluster IV, providing a potential mechanistic basis for antigen cross-presentation. Incorporation of PfHSP70-3-SBD enhanced PfCSP-specific total IgG responses and increased IFN-gamma expression in BALB/c mice, indicating improved immunogenicity upon co-formulation. Notably, immune sera neutralized Pb/Pf CSP sporozoites, delaying blood-stage patency until day 12 in 40% of C57BL/6 mice, with no detectable parasitemia in surviving mice for up to 2 months, indicating sustained efficacy against the sporozoite stage. Interpretation: Molecular chaperones, including HSPs, are currently under intense investigation for their immune-potentiating activity, leading to next-generation vaccine development. By utilizing chaperonic domains derived directly from the pathogenic agent itself to serve an essential adjuvant function, this approach reduces reliance on heterologous adjuvants while enhancing antigen-specific immunity. Funding: This work was supported by funding from Indian Council of Medical Research (IIRPSG-2024-01-03940). Keywords: Substrate-binding domain, PfHSP70-3, Adjuvant, Cross-presentation, Pre-erythrocytic stage, Plasmodium falciparum

items.title: High Burden of Multidrug Resistance and β-Lactamase-Associated Resistance Phenotypes among Gram-Negative Bacilli in Regional Healthcare Facilities in Northern Tanzania
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Gram-negative bacteria threatens effective treatment of bacterial infections, yet data from regional healthcare facilities in Tanzania remain limited. β-lactamase-associated resistance further constrains therapeutic options. Objective To determine antimicrobial resistance patterns and the prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-associated resistance, and AmpC-associated resistance phenotypes among clinical Gram-negative bacterial isolates from two healthcare facilities in Manyara Region, Tanzania. Methods A laboratory-based cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2025 to June 2026 at Manyara Regional Referral Hospital and Haydom Lutheran Hospital. A total of 370 non-duplicate Gram-negative bacterial isolates were included. Bacterial identification was performed using conventional biochemical methods and API identification systems. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby–Bauer disk diffusion method according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. ESBL- and AmpC-associated resistance were assessed phenotypically. MDR and XDR were classified according to internationally accepted criteria. Results Escherichia coli (37.3%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (23.8%) predominated. Resistance was highest to ampicillin (82.7%), cefoxitin (72.7%), and trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole (72.2%), while carbapenem resistance was lower for imipenem (10.5%) and meropenem (6.2%). Overall, 292 (79.0%) isolates were MDR and 178 (48.1%) were XDR. MDR was highest among Acinetobacter baumannii (93.8%) and K. pneumoniae (89.8%), while XDR was highest among A. baumannii (75.0%) and K. pneumoniae (72.7%). ESBL-associated resistance was observed in 64/315 (20.3%) Enterobacterales isolates, while phenotypic AmpC-associated resistance occurred in 148/370 (40.0%) isolates and inducible AmpC-associated resistance in 34/370 (9.2%). Among Enterobacterales, ESBL-associated resistance and constitutive AmpC-associated resistance were significantly associated with MDR ( p = 0.027 and p = 0.046, respectively), whereas inducible AmpC-associated resistance was not ( p = 0.727). Conclusion Regional healthcare facilities in Manyara showed a substantial burden of MDR, XDR, and β-lactamase-associated resistance phenotypes. Strengthening laboratory-based AMR surveillance, facility-specific antibiograms, antimicrobial stewardship, and infection prevention and control is warranted.

items.title: Development of a Foundation AI-Based Multimodal Human Machine Interaction Framework for Intelligent Accelerometer-Assisted Robotic Hand Glove Control in Parkinson's Disease
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract This study proposes a Foundation Artificial Intelligence (Foundation AI)-based multimodal human–machine interaction framework for an intelligent accelerometer-assisted robotic hand glove to support personalized upper-limb rehabilitation in Parkinson's disease patients. Approximately 150 participants (120 Parkinson's disease patients with Hoehn and Yahr Stage II–III and 30 healthy elderly volunteers) perform six clinically relevant Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), including grasping, eating, drinking, writing, dressing, and opening doors, to capture realistic neuromuscular movement patterns. The lightweight soft robotic glove integrates surface EMG sensors, an IMU incorporating a three-axis accelerometer and gyroscope, flex sensors, force-sensitive resistors, pressure sensors, vibration sensors, and temperature sensors to continuously monitor muscle activity, hand kinematics, tremor characteristics, grip force, wrist orientation, and movement acceleration. The embedded accelerometer enhances movement intention recognition by detecting motion direction, velocity, posture transitions, and dynamic hand activities. To improve accessibility, the framework incorporates three intelligent human–machine interaction modules: voice command control using Whisper and a Bidirectional Transformer for speech-driven robotic assistance; vision-based control via an external webcam, employing MediaPipe Hands for real-time hand landmark detection and Vision Transformer (ViT) for gesture recognition and movement intention estimation; and a mobile healthcare platform supporting personalized rehabilitation, remote monitoring, and secure telemedicine communication through Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), MQTT, and AES-256 encryption. The visual features extracted from the webcam are fused with multimodal physiological and motion signals through a Multimodal Foundation Transformer (MFT) incorporating cross-modal attention and self-supervised contrastive learning to estimate movement intention, tremor severity, hand gesture, finger trajectory, grasp type, and grip force. An Adaptive Impedance Controller subsequently personalizes robotic assistance by regulating actuator torque, finger motion, and wrist orientation in real time while continuously adapting to patient-specific neuromuscular conditions. The proposed framework establishes an intelligent multimodal perception and control architecture for personalized robotic rehabilitation and provides the computational foundation for future Digital Twin-enabled adaptive neuro-rehabilitation.

items.title: Antifungal Activity of Natural Compounds and Therapeutic Potential of Allicin–Cinnamaldehyde Combination Against Pet Malassezia Pachydermatis
items.abstract_or_text: Malassezia is a common fungus and one of the zoonotic pathogens. It is a common disease among pets including cats, which usually parasitizes the skin surfaces under suitable environmental conditions. Management of Malassezia dermatitis relies mainly on antifungal drugs. Repeated or prolonged usage may be accompanied by reduced susceptibility and concerns about recurrence. Natural compounds may offer advantages in the management of superficial fungal skin disease. In this study, thirty-eight clinical samples were collected from pet cats with Malassezia-associated skin lesions and a KM mouse dermatitis model was established for in vivo evaluation. Three M. pachydermatis isolates were screened against 11 antibiotics and 14 natural compounds. The most resistant Malassezia pachydermis strain SZ06 was selected for minimum inhibitory concentration determination using checkerboard assays, growth-curve analysis, scanning electron microscopy after treatment, and genome annotation. Plant-derived compound allicin, cinnamaldehyde, eugenol, and anisaldehyde showed significant antifungal activity. Checkerboard assays showed the strongest synergistic effect for allicin plus cinnamaldehyde, reducing the minimum inhibitory concentrations of allicin and cinnamaldehyde to one-eighth and one-quarter of their single-agent values, respectively. For the regression mice infected with SZ06, topical treatment with 0.5% allicin plus 0.5% cinnamaldehyde produced the best therapeutic response, improving lesions, fungal clearance, histopathology, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Genome sequencing of SZ06 suggested that this isolate carried multiple candidate genes involved in efflux, membrane transport, and drug-response pathways. The natural compound allicin-cinnamaldehyde combination demonstrated promising antifungal activity, representing a potential topical therapy for Malassezia dermatitis in pet cats.

items.title: Calibration, Uncertainty, and Data Efficiency of Deep Learning Chest Radiograph Classifiers Under Cross-Dataset Distribution Shift: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark
items.abstract_or_text: Purpose To evaluate the external transportability of source-derived probability calibration for chest radiograph deep learning classifiers under distribution shift and determine its dependence on sample size and disease prevalence. Materials and Methods This retrospective secondary computational analysis of public, de-identified radiographic datasets involved no participant contact or new data collection. Cohort sizes were prespecified by availability without prospective power calculation: 106,686 NIH ChestX-ray14 images (29,323 patients; 1992-2015) for development and internal testing, 20,000 CheXpert images (20,000 patients; October 2002-July 2017), and 14,998 VinBigData images (2018-2020) for external testing. ResNet-18, DenseNet-121, and DeiT-Tiny classifiers for cardiomegaly and pleural effusion were trained across four patient fractions and three seeds (36 fits). Calibrators were fitted exclusively on NIH data. Twelve primary external Brier-score contrasts (temperature-scaled versus raw probabilities) were evaluated using paired cluster-bootstrapping with Holm adjustment. Results Temperature scaling reduced Brier scores in nine of 12 primary contrasts but worsened pleural effusion calibration on VinBigData across all architectures (Brier increases: ResNet-18, 0.001460 [95% CI: 0.001347, 0.001568]; DenseNet-121, 0.001193 [95% CI: 0.001109, 0.001274]; DeiT-Tiny, 0.000498 [95% CI: 0.000417, 0.000577]; all adjusted P=.006). Standardizing class weights to NIH prevalence reversed all CheXpert improvements. Although full versus 10% training improved external AUROC across all comparisons, DeiT-Tiny CheXpert pleural effusion Brier score worsened by 0.007039 despite a 0.032466 AUROC gain. At 80% selective image retention, calibrated ensembles retained only 12.3%-17.2% of VinBigData positive pleural effusion examinations. Conclusion Source-fitted calibration is not uniformly transportable across health systems, and discrimination gains do not guarantee calibrated probabilities. External evaluation must simultaneously assess probability reliability, prevalence shifts, and retained-case composition.

items.title: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf72-FTLD
items.abstract_or_text: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers (n=72) and non-carriers (n=48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72-associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1, a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD.

items.title: Cuproptosis: Biochemical Mechanisms, Therapeutic Potential, and Clinical Challenges
items.abstract_or_text: Cuproptosis is a novel form of regulated cell death, discovered in 2022, that occurs due to excessive copper accumulation in mitochondria. Unlike apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis, cuproptosis depends on lipoylation of TCA cycle proteins, particularly DLAT, mediated by FDX1, and is accompanied by aggregation of lipoylated proteins and loss of Fe-S cluster proteins. This essay critically reviews the biochemical mechanisms of cuproptosis, its dual role in carcinogenesis (cuproplasia vs. cuproptosis), as well as its involvement in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and musculoskeletal diseases. Therapeutic strategies are considered: copper ionophores (elesclomol, disulfiram), chelators (TTM, D-penicillamine), and nanotechnological delivery systems. Despite its substantial therapeutic potential, the clinical translation of cuproptosis-targeted strategies remains constrained by the lack of specific biomarkers, the complexity of selectivity control, and contradictory results of clinical trials. The need for biomarker-guided stratification of patients (e.g., by LDH level, FDX1 expression, ARID1A mutation status) and the development of tumor-specific nanosystems to minimize systemic toxicity are substantiated. The central thesis posits that cuproptosis is not merely a novel form of cell death, but a fundamental biochemical switch revealing the dual nature of copper; however, its clinical translation hinges on overcoming key limitations (Figure 1).

items.title: A new mouse model for a high-risk AMD variant, ARMS2A69S
items.abstract_or_text: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of irreversible central vision loss in older adults. The highest genetic risk for AMD maps to Chromosome 10q26. However, due to strong linkage disequilibrium between two genes, ARMS2 and HTRA1 located in this region, it has been difficult to determine whether one or both genes contribute to the AMD-disease risk. Functional studies of ARMS2 have been hampered due to the lack of animal models, as orthologs are only found in the higher primates and the gene is absent in rodents. To model ARMS2 biology in vivo, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to insert the complete human ARMS2 gene carrying the A69S risk variant (rs10490924), into a region of homology between humans and mice, on mouse Chromosome 7, 3.5 kb upstream of Htra1, preserving its native promoter, spacing, and orientation. We also generated a mouse model bearing its wild-type counterpart ARMS2A69 (ARMS2WT). RNA analysis revealed tissue- and cell-type-specific pattern of ARMS2 expression enriched in neural tissues, testis, and eye, and within the eye, in retinal horizontal cells and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). ARMS2 expression was consistent with human expression data and unaltered by the A69S mutation. By 12 months, ARMS2A69S mice develop AMD-relevant phenotypes including increased fundus spots, A69S-specific thinning of the outer nuclear layer, and reduced scotopic ERG amplitudes. Transcriptomic profiling of postnatal day 14 retina and RPE-enriched fractions revealed reduced mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation genes, corroborated by reduced retinal mtDNA copy number and lower maximal respiration, alongside preliminary results that suggest sphingolipid remodeling in the RPE. This humanized model links the ARMS2 A69S variant to mitochondrial dysfunction and provides an in vivo platform for defining AMD mechanisms and testing therapies.

items.title: Facilitating Valid Statistical Inference in Biomedical Image Synthesis
items.abstract_or_text: Generative AI for medical image synthesis is increasingly used to impute missing data and augment biomedical datasets. Yet despite achieving high computational similarity to their real-world counterparts, synthetic images remain uncommon in clinical research practice, in part because of concerns about their biological validity. Here, we evaluate whether synthetic images support reliable downstream statistical analysis and biological inference in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and multiplexed immunofluorescence (mIF) imaging. We find that associations between patient phenotypes and synthesized images can be severely attenuated. This is because synthesis methods typically omit clinically relevant covariates and therefore generate images that, although visually realistic, mask key biological differences. Furthermore, naive analyses treat synthesized images as if they were observed, ignoring the statistical uncertainty introduced by synthesis. Drawing on multiple imputation theory, we introduce Phenotype Aware Multiple Synthesis (PAMS), an analysis framework that requires no model retraining and instead adjusts synthesized output to recover valid biological estimates with appropriately calibrated uncertainty. Applied to MRI and mIF data, PAMS reduced estimation bias and restored nominal confidence interval coverage. Because it is compatible with existing synthesis pipelines, PAMS offers a practical and rigorous route to statistically and biologically valid use of synthesized images in biomedical imaging research.

items.title: Performance evaluation and benchmarking across 16 large language model configurations on a large real-world emergency department triage data set
items.abstract_or_text: Background Emergency department (ED) triage is a decision process that determines patient prioritization and resource allocation. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as decision-support tools for triage, yet most evaluations rely on curated datasets. Evidence from real-world clinical environments remains limited. The objective of this project was to evaluate the performance and reproducibility of multiple contemporary large language models for Emergency Severity Index (ESI) classification and sectoral allocation (ED vs. urgent care practice, UCP) using a real-world triage dataset. Material and Methods Retrospective cross-sectional benchmarking study conducted at a tertiary academic ED in Germany with an integrated central point of assessment (CPA). The study included all 16,107 walk-in encounters between October 18, 2023, and February 27, 2024. Sixteen configurations were compared on the first 2,000 encounters; GPT 5.1 with high reasoning effort was additionally evaluated on all 16,107 encounters. Data were collected from a structured clinical decision support system capturing presenting complaints, vital signs, and triage decisions recorded by specialized nursing staff. Results The primary outcome was the agreement between LLM-predicted and nurse-assigned ESI levels measured using quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa. Secondary outcomes included sectoral assignment agreement, misclassification patterns (over- and under-triage), confidence-agreement comparisons, and output reproducibility. In the primary analysis of all 16,107 encounters, GPT 5.1 with high reasoning effort achieved quadratic-weighted kappa = 0.5031 (95% CI 0.4904-0.5158). In the exploratory comparison of 16 configurations on the shared 2,000-encounter subset, quadratic-weighted kappa ranged from 0.180 to 0.860. The Stepwise approach, combining structured model assessments with deterministic ESI mapping, achieved quadratic-weighted kappa = 0.860 (95% CI 0.841-0.878) and 82.70% exact agreement. Most models demonstrated moderate or lower agreement. Sectoral assignment agreement (i.e. ED vs. urgent care practice, UCP) was uniformly low (kappa of 0.304 or lower). Reproducibility testing revealed substantial variability in 23% of cases, indicating non-deterministic output behavior for clinically relevant decisions. Conclusions Current large language models demonstrate heterogeneous and generally limited performance in real-world emergency triage tasks. The Stepwise approach achieved the highest agreement. Before clinical implementation, confidence estimates, reliability, and workflow integration require prospective validation in regulatory-compliant clinical settings.

items.title: Temporal multi-omics dataset of a cucurbit–powdery mildew interaction
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Plant-pathogenic fungi are major contributors to global crop losses, yet many of the most damaging groups, especially obligate biotrophs, remain difficult to study. Their strict dependence on living host tissue limits experimental manipulation and has constrained the generation of comprehensive datasets that capture how these pathogens suppress host immunity and reprogram metabolism over time. To expand the resources available for data-driven research, we present a temporally resolved multi-omics dataset characterizing the interaction between Cucumis melo and Podosphaera xanthii , the causal agent of cucurbit powdery mildew and a model obligate biotroph. Inoculated and mock-treated melon leaves were sampled across 12 time points from 12 to 144 hours post inoculation, covering key developmental transitions of the pathogen. The dataset integrates dual RNA-seq and untargeted LC–MS/MS metabolomics generated from the same biological material, accompanied by detailed documentation of experimental design, bioinformatic workflows, quality-control metrics and processed outputs to ensure broad reusability. This resource enables exploration of host–pathogen transcriptional dynamics, stage-specific infection responses, metabolic remodeling and integrative multi-omics analyses of obligate biotrophy.

items.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models (LLMs) or Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), combining feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing and calibration, and confidence-gated training self-conditioning. LangDiT significantly reduces generation perplexity in matched LangFlow comparisons, establishing a new state of the art in continuous language generation across different model formulations. Using LangFlow as a representative CDLM, LangDiT as a plug-and-play backbone leads to a new state-of-the-art model with a generation perplexity (GenPPL) of 21.72 using 1024 NFEs and 44.72 GenPPL using 128 NFEs on the unconditional generation of 1024-token sequences on the OpenWebText dataset. When adapted to Plaid-style CDLM formulations, LangDiT results in a new leading GenPPL of 11.33 using 1024 denoising NFEs, and 27.51 GenPPL using 128 denoising NFEs. These gains are achieved while retaining each model's underlying representation, training objective, and inference sampler, isolating transformer architecture as a fundamental source of improvement. Our study identifies architectural design as an important source of improvement in continuous diffusion language models.

items.title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
items.abstract_or_text: Large language models (LLMs) can generate differential diagnoses for complex cases, but a useful second opinion must also be factually grounded, clinically coherent, actionable, and safe. We developed a multidimensional benchmark using 300 diagnostically resolved NEJM--MedQA cases: 110 for physician reference ratings and Judge calibration and 190 for held-out evaluation. Eight single-model pipelines generated independent role-specific opinions and interactive-consilium reports under free-form and structured clinical-reasoning conditions. A physician-calibrated LLM Judge evaluated 3,040 final reports and the corresponding structured primary-role outputs. Model identity separated report quality more strongly than response format. Structured final reports had higher overall mean scores in seven of eight model pipelines, with their clearest advantage in management (2.740 vs. 2.436). Compared with the structured pre-consilium primary-role opinion, the complete structured synthesis had higher pooled scores across all five shared criteria, with the largest increases in problem prioritization, factual grounding, and reasoning coherence. GPT-5.6-Sol led every evaluated component and reached consensus in the fewest review rounds. These findings show that the benchmark can distinguish model capability, the contribution of multidisciplinary synthesis, criterion-specific effects of response structure, deliberation dynamics, and inference requirements within one common-case evaluation.

items.title: DuET: Note-Frame Dual Encoding for Piano Performance-to-Score Transcription
items.abstract_or_text: Transcribing expressive piano performances into scores requires interpreting individual note timings within an underlying metrical structure. However, score attributes are associated with notes, whereas beats may occur without coincident note onsets. We introduce DuET, a Dual-Encoder Transformer that jointly learns note-level performance MIDI-to-score (PM2S) transcription and frame-level beat and downbeat tracking. Bidirectional cross-attention connects note and frame encoders, while an autoregressive decoder alternates between their representations to predict structured score attributes. We further introduce TimeRoPE and Time-Pitch Rotary Positional Encoding (TPRoPE) to establish a shared performance-time reference and explicitly encode relative temporal and pitch relationships. Evaluations on ASAP, a classical piano dataset, and our curated Gangqinpu dataset, which spans multiple genres with a focus on popular piano music, demonstrate improvements in score timing and notated duration. Compared with the strongest baseline on each dataset, DuET reduces MUSTER mean error from 6.56% to 3.64% on Gangqinpu and from 11.30% to 11.22% on ASAP. Ablations support the benefits of frame-level context, time-based positional encoding, and decoder-history masking. Code, weights, and demos are available at https://github.com/wei-zeng98/DuET.

items.title: Incentivizing Tool-Use Reinforcement Learning for Post-Arrival Emergency Care Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Large language models (LLMs) can reason over both structured measurements and free-text records, which makes them attractive for emergency department (ED) prediction. However, most existing LLMs still fall short of conventional ML methods like trees on EHR-based prediction tasks. Our controlled analysis traces this gap to two weaknesses: LLMs do not select informative features, and they misjudge what numerical values imply for risk even when given the right features. We propose TIR-EC, a tool-integrated reinforcement learning framework that addresses both. TIR-EC exposes EHR feature groups as tools the LLM can call. It trains the LLM with rewards from a gradient-boosted tree teacher, which provides a reference set of informative tools and a graded risk target. TIR-EC also distills task-specific clinical skills into the model weights through a reverse curriculum that gradually removes the skills from the prompt during RL process. Evaluation on three clinical prediction tasks shows that our 4B agent achieves the highest macro F1 of all compared models, outperforms conventional ML baselines, and is competitive with much larger frontier LLMs. Further analysis shows that TIR-EC selects more useful evidence with fewer tool calls and combines measurements more effectively.

items.title: AutoOnboarder: Autonomously Onboarding LLM Agents
items.abstract_or_text: Agentic large language models have been documented to lose reasoning capability when placed inside a harness, the software that mediates their observations and actions. To reconcile these losses, we introduce AutoOnboarder, an autonomous system that adapts an agent to a task the way a trainer onboards a new employee. It places the agent under the supervision of an intelligent ``Onboarder'' coding agent, which iteratively tailors its foundation model, prompt, and harness source code to simultaneously improve performance and decrease cost. Like a real onboarding process, the Onboarder is only given tens of examples, and all evaluation data is isolated on a separate virtual machine to prevent leakage. We report the lessons learned from building and testing AutoOnboarder on genomic-sequencing prior authorization form submission. Autonomously onboarded agents are able to match or exceed the performance of a Gemini 3.5 Flash baseline at up to 29\times lower costs. However, these agents remain imperfect, and the Onboarding process varies greatly in terms of final performance. We conclude that future Onboarding systems require a robust environment for the Onboarder, including a structured thought interface, (controlled) internet access, and a wide model search space.

items.title: PatientPheX: A Full-Text Biomedical Corpus for Patient-Specific Phenotype Information Extraction
items.abstract_or_text: Patient-specific phenotype information extraction identifiers and normalizes phenotype entities and links them with individual patients, supporting rare disease research and genotype-phenotype analysis. However, existing datasets rarely combine full-text biomedical content with detailed annotations of patients, phenotypes, related entities, and their associations. In this work, we present PatientPheX, a corpus for patient-specific phenotype information extraction comprising 200 full-text articles, primarily case reports and case series. The corpus provides mention annotations and normalization for seven biomedical entity types, together with explicit associations between patients and entities across sentences, paragraphs, and sections. Negated findings and composite phenotype mentions are also annotated. Corpus construction combines automated pre-annotation, large language model (LLM)-assisted verification, and manual review and adjudication. Benchmarks cover entity recognition and normalization and patient-phenotype association extraction using gold-standard and predicted entities. The overall document-level entity F1 was 86.95%, while phenotype F1 was 79.33%. The best relation extraction macro-F1 decreased from 84.14% with gold-standard entities to 54.98% with predicted entities, highlighting the combined challenges of phenotype extraction and patient attribution. PatientPheX provides a resource for developing and evaluating patient-centered information extraction methods and supports the construction of structured patient-level knowledge resources for phenotype-driven biomedical research.

items.title: Determining cellular phylogeny and migration at high resolution in spatial genomics
items.abstract_or_text: Cellular migration and tumor evolution are central to tissue homeostasis and cancer biology. Rapid advances in spatial genomics have raised the possibility of using somatic mutations to track these processes in situ in human tissues. However, frequent data dropouts in spatial genomics measurements make this challenging to implement. Here, we present StarTrak (SpaTial Analysis for lineage ReconsTRuction with somatic vAriant calling and tracKing), a framework for somatic variant calling and lineage reconstruction at single-pixel spatial resolution. StarTrak employs a neural network framework to integrate mutational evidence (from both nuclear and mitochondrial reads), spatial proximity, histological images, and transcriptomic states to identify spatially informative patterns of mutations. It performs robustly across tissue types and spatial-omics platforms (being particularly successful with spatial ATAC-seq). Applying StarTrak to tumor sections, we infer the migration of mutated tumor cells into adjacent non-malignant tissues and reconstruct distinct lineage trees associated with different spatial regions. Notably, we identify tumor regions with nearly identical transcriptomic states but distinct mutational profiles. Moreover, for skin sections, StarTrak identifies sunlight-associated mutations in non-malignant epidermis and evidence suggesting the migration of these mutant surface cells into deeper skin layers. Overall, by integrating mutation calling with spatial context, StarTrak enables the inference of spatially resolved cellular migration and cellular phylogeny.

items.title: A relational architecture of the human genome
